Jesus therefore being wearied with <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> journey, sat thus on the well <ns0:note n="k." place="bottom">Our Lord used no Horse, or Chariot ordinarily in his Travels, but went on foot; we never read of him in a Coach or Chariot, but once upon the back of a beast, (that was when he rode into <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> upon an Ass) he ordinarily travelled on foot; and the Evangelist taketh no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tice of his weariness, to let us know that he was truly Man, and subjected to <ns0:hi>weariness,</ns0:hi> and other humane infirmities; and he rested himself upon the sides of the Well</ns0:note>: and it was about the sixth hour <ns0:note n="l," place="bottom">and it was about Noon-time: For that was according to their computation, the sixth hour. The 8th Verse tells us, His Disciples were gone to the City to buy Meat, so as he was alone.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">It is uncertain, whether this woman was a Citizen of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> which City is said to be at two miles distance from this place, or one of that Country, which went by that Name, (for <ns0:hi>Samaria</ns0:hi> was the Name of that Region, as well as of a City); she came not out of any design to meet with Christ there, but came to draw water; they having not Pumps and Wells so common as we have, were forced to travel for Water for their necessary uses. Thus it often happeneth, that we meet with Divine Mercy when we think not of it. God is found of those who seek him not, nor inquire after him, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 65.1. which lets us see how all our motions and actions are at the Divine dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posal and government. <ns0:hi>Rachel</ns0:hi> went not to the Well, to meet with the Tidings of an Husband, but to water her Fathers flock; but yet there she met with <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> Gen. 29.9. as it had happened to <ns0:hi>Rebecca</ns0:hi> before, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 24.15. This Woman (as appeareth by what followeth) was no better than an Harlot; to her Christ (fleeing from the Pharisees, the great Doctors of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>) bringeth the <ns0:hi>glad tidings</ns0:hi> of the Gospel, and she receives them. So admirab<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e are the Dispensations of Divine Providence</ns0:note>: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink <ns0:note n="n:" place="bottom">He prevents this wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man, saying unto her, <ns0:hi>Give me to drink.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For his disciples were gone away into the city to buy meat <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">This is added, lest any should say, How came our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour in this discourse with the woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria?</ns0:hi> They were travelling upon the Road, and came near to <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi>: Our Lords Disciples were gone to the city to buy some Food for them; in the mean time, our Saviour coming to the <ns0:hi>Well,</ns0:hi> called <ns0:hi>Iacobs Well,</ns0:hi> sets him down, and this <ns0:hi>Sama<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritan-woman</ns0:hi> cometh to that Well, to <ns0:hi>draw Water.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour being thirsty, asks of her some Water to drink; this giveth occasion to the following Discourse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:335" />9 Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it, that thou being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a woman of Samaria <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">There was a great estrangement of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> having a peculiar Temple built upon mount <ns0:hi>Gerazim,</ns0:hi> in opposition to that at <ns0:hi>Hieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem q.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>? for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 King. 17.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>4. Luk. 9.52, 53. Acts 10.28.</ns0:note> the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans <ns0:note n="q." place="bottom">It is said that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> did buy of, and sell to the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> but were restrained by an Order of the <ns0:hi>Sanhedrim,</ns0:hi> from using any familiarity with them, or bor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rowing or receiving any thing as a Gift from them, which was the cause of this Reply of the woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> knowing our Saviour either by his Habit, or by his Dialect, to be a <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi>; this is thought to be the sense of <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in this Text, though it hath a larger significancy, extend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to all kind of Commerce.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Jesus answered, and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Many by the <ns0:hi>gift of God</ns0:hi> here understand <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> whom God gave to the World, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.16. And who is the great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est Gift that God ever gave to the World; so as the latter words, <ns0:hi>and who it is,</ns0:hi> &c. expound the former</ns0:note>, and who it is that saith unto thee, Give me to drink, thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 2.13.</ns0:note> li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving water <ns0:note n="s." place="bottom">Thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee either a true knowledge of the Doctrine, or the Grace tendered in the Gospel, or the holy Spirit, called <ns0:hi>water,</ns0:hi> because it washeth and cleanseth the Soul; and <ns0:hi>living water,</ns0:hi> because it is always running and flowing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that living water <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">What our Saviour spake <ns0:hi>metaphorically,</ns0:hi> comparing his Grace, or his Spirit, or the Doctrine of his Gospel to Living Water, this poor woman understandeth <ns0:hi>literally</ns0:hi>; and know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing that the Well was very deep, (some say forty cubits) and seeing him as a Traveller, not provided with any thing to draw with, or into; she asks him, Whence he had that Living water? a Question much like that of <ns0:hi>Nicodemus, ch.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. So ignorant are persons of spiritual things, till they be enlightened by the holy Spirit of God.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Art thou greater then our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattel <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">She asks him, if he judged himself wiser than <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> whom she calleth their Father? It is often observed, that the <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> would ordinarily claim Kindred with the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> when the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were in prosperity; but in their ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versity, constantly disowned any relation to them. There were some <ns0:hi>Iews (Ephraimites</ns0:hi> especially) mixt with a far greater number of <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> which made up this Body of People called the <ns0:hi>Samaritans.</ns0:hi> Now saith the <ns0:hi>Woman, Iacob</ns0:hi> who was the Father of <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> from whom we claim, was a wise Man, and he could find no better Water hereabouts for himself and family, than that of this Well; art thou wiser than he?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Jesus answered and said unto her, Whoso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ever drinketh of this water, shall thirst again <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Our Saviour in his Reply justifieth the excellency of that <ns0:hi>living water,</ns0:hi> which he had before declared to be in his power to give, and his readiness to have given to this woman, if she had asked it of him, from the perishing virtue of the Water of this Well; and the continuing virtue of his <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> which he compared to this Living Water: No man so asswaged his Thirst by drinking of the Water of <ns0:hi>Iacobs Well,</ns0:hi> but he was subject to thirst again.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.35, 54.</ns0:note> whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.38.</ns0:note>, shall never thirst <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">But he who receiveth the holy Spirit, and the Grace thereof, though he will be daily saying, <ns0:hi>Give, give,</ns0:hi> and be continually desiring further supplies of Grace, yet he shall never wholly want, never want any good thing that shall be necessary for him, the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eed of God shall abide in him</ns0:note>: but the wa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter that I shall give him, shall be in him a well of water, springing up into everlasting life <ns0:note n="y," place="bottom">and this Water shall be in him a <ns0:hi>spring</ns0:hi> of Water, supplying him until he come to Heaven. But this Text was excel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lently expounded by our Saviour, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.38, 39. <ns0:hi>He that be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieveth on me</ns0:hi> (as the Scripture hath said) out of his <ns0:hi>belly shall flow rivers of living water,</ns0:hi> v. 39. <ns0:hi>But this speaketh he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him, should receive.</ns0:hi> From which it is plain, that our Saviour here by the <ns0:hi>living water</ns0:hi> he speaketh of, understood the <ns0:hi>holy Spirit.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> thirst not, neither come hither to draw <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">I am not of their mind, who think that this woman understood our Saviour, speaking about <ns0:hi>spiritual water,</ns0:hi> only had a mind to talk; and indeed, it is hard to conceive, how a woman of her education, and way of life, should un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand any such thing; but it is plain, that she did not understand him in what he was discoursing about, but doth as it were, deride him, believing that he had no such thing to bestow: She taketh no notice of the Water which our Saviour had spoken of, springing up to eternal life, but re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />garding only the present life, and her ease in that, and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sires favour of Christ only to supply her wants in this life, and that she might live at more ease; so true is that of the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.5. Thus, <ns0:hi>they that are after the flesh, do mind the things of the flesh.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Not that Christ did not know what she afterward confest, that she lived in Whoredom, and had no Legiti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mate Husband: But he said this probably, to check her pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tulancy, and mocking, at what he spake about the <ns0:hi>living water,</ns0:hi> and to bring her to a sense of her sin, that she might be more fit to receive the glad tidings of a Saviour, which he was about to publish to her; and this seems rather to be our Saviours design, in bidding her go call her Husband, than (as some of the Ancients thought) that he might bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter instruct her, or avoid any scandal to himself, by a longer private discourse with a woman alone, who was of no better Reputation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 The woman answered, and said, I have no husband <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">That is, none who is my lawful Husband; she denieth not that she had one, whom she used, and lived with as an Husband, but that she had any legal Husband, to whom the clave, and to no other; still she goeth on, thinking to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive Christ, and to put tricks upon him</ns0:note>. Jesus answered, and said, Thou hast well said, I have no husband <ns0:note n="c." place="bottom">Christ tells her, she in this did speak truth; he knew she had no legal Husband.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 For thou hast had five husbands, and he whom thou now hast, is not thy husband <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He tells her, that she had <ns0:hi>five Husbands,</ns0:hi> whether suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessively, the former being dead, and she marrying another: or five from whom she had been divorced for Adultery, is not agreed; the best modern Interpreters judg, that she had had five m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n, to whom she had been in Marriage, but so behaved her self toward them, that either for her Adul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tery, or some other froward behaviour towards them, they had given her a Bill of Divorce</ns0:note>: in that saidst thou truly <ns0:note n="e;" place="bottom">and tho she now used, and lived with one as her Husband, yet in this she said truly, because her former Husbands yet living, he was not her Husband: This seemeth more properly the sense, than that after five legal Husbands death, she lived in whoredom with a sixth person. By this discovery, our Saviour both bring<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth her to the sense of her sin, and also to an acknowledg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of him as the Messiah.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 The woman saith unto him <ns0:note place="margin">Luk. 7.16. & 24.19. Chap. 6.14.</ns0:note>, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Whose Office is to reveal the will of God, and to whom God revealeth secret things. One to whom the Lord maketh known himself in a Vision, and speaketh in a Dream, <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 12.6. The womans Reply seemeth to signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fie both: Her acknowledgment of Christ as a <ns0:hi>Prophe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> upon his telling her secret things, justifieth her looking upon him, as one to whom God revealed things not known or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinarily to men; and that this report of her meaning ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth by what she said, <ns0:hi>vers.</ns0:hi> 9. to her Fellow-Citizens, <ns0:hi>Come see a man which hath told me all things that ever I did:</ns0:hi> but the following Verse, in which she entreth into a discouese with our Saviour, about the Controversie be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Samaritans about Worship,</ns0:hi> lets us know, that she looked upon him as a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> in the more ordinary sense, as <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> signifies one influenced by God, to reveal his mind and will unto Men; and indeed, there was no <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> in the former sense, but was also in the latter; tho there were many <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> in the latter sense, sent of God, and enabled to reveal the will of God unto Men, who were not influenced so far, as to foretel things to come. The difference betwixt an Hypocrite, and one truly brought to a sense of Sin, is very conspicuous in the example of this Woman; she doth not deny her sin, as <ns0:hi>Cain, Gehazi,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ananias</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Saphira</ns0:hi>; neither doth she disco<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver any anger upon the discovery of it, as the <ns0:hi>Scribes and Pharisees,</ns0:hi> the wicked Princes of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rod</ns0:hi> did: Neither doth she go about to excuse or mitigate her sin, but she applieth her self to Christ as a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> to teach her what to do. The example also of this Woman, informs us what use we ought to make of <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> to guide us into the right way, and faithfully to acquaint us with the will of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:336" />20 Our Fathers worshipped in this Mountain <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The Mount <ns0:hi>Gerezim,</ns0:hi> which was an exceeding high Mountain, and near unto <ns0:hi>Sichem. Iacob</ns0:hi> made an Altar thereabouts, which he called <ns0:hi>El-Elohe-Israel,</ns0:hi> Gen. 33.20. Some say, that it was upon that Mountain that <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> should have Offered up <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> Gen. 22. but that had ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther name. Certain it is, that from that Mountain <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> pronounced the <ns0:hi>Blessings,</ns0:hi> Deut. 27.12. But it is very pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bable that the Woman had respect to none of these, but to the common usage of the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> to Worship in a Temple built, upon this Mountain, in opposition to that at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>: The story of which will be very proper here to relate, for the full understanding of this Text. <ns0:hi>San<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ballat</ns0:hi> was Governour of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> Constituted by <ns0:hi>Darius</ns0:hi>; of this <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> we read in <ns0:hi>Nehemiah,</ns0:hi> who tells us that <ns0:hi>One of the Sons</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Eliashib</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> was Son-in-law to this <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Horonite, wherefore I chased him from me,</ns0:hi> Neh. 13.28. This Son-in-law's Name (as <ns0:hi>Iosephus</ns0:hi> tells us) was <ns0:hi>Manasses.</ns0:hi> He was driven out of <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> upon the account of the Covenant made, <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 10.3. That those who had Married strange Wives would turn them away. The Sacred story here leaving us, we must supply it out of <ns0:hi>Iosephus,</ns0:hi> who, <ns0:hi>Antiq. l.</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>cap.</ns0:hi> 8. tells us, that he being thus driven from the Sacrifice, applyed himself to <ns0:hi>Sanballat,</ns0:hi> and would have put his Wife away, which was <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi>'s Daughter; but <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> promised him, that if he would keep his Daughter as his Wife, he would not only continue him in the Priesthood, but make him an <ns0:hi>High-Priest,</ns0:hi> and build him a <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> like that at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> upon Mount <ns0:hi>Gerezim,</ns0:hi> with the leave of <ns0:hi>Darius</ns0:hi>; upon this, <ns0:hi>Manasses</ns0:hi> staid with <ns0:hi>Sanballat,</ns0:hi> and there also resorted many to him whom <ns0:hi>Nehemiah</ns0:hi> had turned out of the Priesthood at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> for Marrying strange Wives. <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> was very near losing his Opportunity through the favour of <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rius,</ns0:hi> by the Conquest of <ns0:hi>Darius</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Alexander</ns0:hi> the Great. But it was regain'd by his Brother <ns0:hi>Iaddus</ns0:hi> his stubbornness, who was <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and refused to own the new Conqueror, which advantage <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> took, and offered <ns0:hi>Alexander</ns0:hi> the surrender of all places in his Trust to him; and being by that means ingratiated with <ns0:hi>Alexan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der</ns0:hi> the Great, he thereby obtained leave of him to build a <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> in Mount <ns0:hi>Gerezim,</ns0:hi> where his Son-in-law <ns0:hi>Manasses</ns0:hi> should be the <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> promising <ns0:hi>Alexander,</ns0:hi> that by this means the force of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would be broken, so as there would be no danger of their Conspiring. Accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ingly he presently built this Temple, and soon after dyed, leaving his Son-in-law <ns0:hi>Manasses,</ns0:hi> Brother to <ns0:hi>Iaddus</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>High Priest,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Hierusalem, High Priest</ns0:hi> in this new <ns0:hi>Temple,</ns0:hi> which afterwards proved an <ns0:hi>Asylum</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sanctuary</ns0:hi> for any who were Accused amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem.</ns0:hi> Thus these two Temples stood for about 220 Years; then <ns0:hi>Hircanus</ns0:hi> an <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> destroyed it; but still they looked upon the Ground as Holy, and came thither to perform their Devotions. With reference to this Super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stitious practice, the <ns0:hi>Woman of Samaria</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Our Fathers Worshipped</ns0:hi> (that is, have used time out of mind to Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship) in this Mountain. And</ns0:note>, and ye say that in <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 12, 6, 11. 1 Kings 9.3. 2 Chron. 7.12.</ns0:note> Hierusalem is the place where men ought to worship <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> hold that none might Worship God by Sacrifice any where but at <ns0:hi>Hieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem,</ns0:hi> according to the Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 12.14, 26.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Woman! thou ownest me as a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> whose Office it is to reveal the will of God unto Men; it is therefore thy Duty to give Credit to what I shall reveal to thee about the true and right way of Worshipping God. The time is coming, yea, at hand, when you shall</ns0:note> when you shall neither in this Mountain <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">neither in this Mount <ns0:hi>Gerezim,</ns0:hi> (where your Fathers have so long Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipped God Superstitiously without any direction from him)</ns0:note>, nor yet at Hierusalem worship the Father <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">nor yet at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> which is the place which the Lord made choice of for his Worship, <ns0:hi>Worship my Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther,</ns0:hi> or your Father. God is putting an end to both these places, and to all that Worship which I shall not Institute under the Gospel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Ye worship <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 17.29.</ns0:note> ye know not what <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">You have no certain Rule for your Worship, but only do things which your Fathers did without any Revelation of the Divine will; by which you may be assured, that what you do is acceptable to God</ns0:note>, we know what we worship <ns0:note n="n." place="bottom">We know that God hath revealed his will, that his People should Worship him at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> by such Rites and Performances as he him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self hath Instituted in his Word, so as we are certain that what we do is acceptable to God</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 9.4, 5.</ns0:note> for Salvation is of the Jews <ns0:note n="o:" place="bottom">For unto the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (of old) were committed the Oracles of God, the ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nary means of Salvation, <ns0:hi>Out of Zion went forth the Law, and the word of the Lord from Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> Isaiah 2.3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit, and in truth <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Under the Gospel, and the Kingdom of the Messiah, which is yet further coming, and is already began in the World, the true Worshippers of God shall not Worship him, as you <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> who Worship you know not what, without any Rule or Prescript of the Word; nor yet as the Hypocritical <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who rest upon their Sacrifices and Ri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual performances, as if they should purge away their sins, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 50.8. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1.11. and 66.3. <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 6.7. no, nor yet as the more sincere <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who indeed do truly and with their Hearts Worship God; but <ns0:hi>while the first Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bernacle was yet standing, which was a Figure for the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent time,</ns0:hi> by Sacrifices <ns0:hi>that could not make him that did the Service perfect as pertaining to the Conscience—by meats, and drinks, and divers Ordinances, imposed on them until the time of Reformation,</ns0:hi> Heb. 9.10. That time of Reformation is now come, when the true Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shippers of God shall offer up to him a more <ns0:hi>Spiritual Worship</ns0:hi>; not that Carnal Worship; and a more true, and real, and solid Worship</ns0:note>: for the Father seeketh such to worship him <ns0:note n="q;" place="bottom">for God my Father seeketh such to Worship him, as shall not Worship him with a mere bodily labour and Homage, but with their Hearts and Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rits; nor with those Ceremonial performances now in use by Gods Prescript at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; but without them, I be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing come, whom all those Services did but pre-figure, and point unto.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 3.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> God <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a Spirit <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">God is not a Corporeal Being, made up of Blood, and Flesh, and Bones, having Senses as Bodies have, to be pleased with sensible things; but he is a Spiritual Being, the Father of Spirits, and requireth a Spiritual Service proportioned to his Being</ns0:note>, and they that worship him, must worship <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> in spirit, and in truth <ns0:note n="s," place="bottom">and therefore those that pay a Religious Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mage to him, must do it with their Spirits, and according to the Rule that he hath prescribed in truth and reality. This is now the will of God; and tho' he required of his People under the Law a more Ritual Figurative Service, yet that is now to cease; and therefore the Woman of <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />maria</ns0:hi> need not trouble her self which was the truest Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship, that at <ns0:hi>Mount Gerazim,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mount Sion,</ns0:hi> for both of them were very suddenly to determine, and a new and more substantial Spiritual Worship was to succeed, to the learning of the way and method of which she was more to attend, and not to spend her thoughts about these things, which were of no significancy, and tended onely to Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster Questions of no use.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 The Woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The Woman by this reply, tho a Woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> sheweth her self to be a <ns0:hi>Iew,</ns0:hi> for she was one of them who lived in an expectation of one whom the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> called the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> Prophecied of by <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> under this Notion, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.25, 26. and by the <ns0:hi>Psalmist, Psal.</ns0:hi> 2.2. which term <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> (that is, <ns0:hi>Anointed</ns0:hi>) in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi>;</ns0:note>, when he is come he will tell us all things <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">she had a further Notion, That this <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> should be a great <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> Deut. 18.15. yea, she appears to have had a further Notion of the <ns0:hi>Messiah, viz.</ns0:hi> that when he came he should reveal to them the whole will of God as to the Salvation of Man, and the Worship of God; this lets us know, that she was none of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> part of the Inhabitants of <ns0:hi>Samaria.</ns0:hi> If any ask, how she, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing a <ns0:hi>Samaritan,</ns0:hi> should know any thing of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> receiving onely the five Books of <ns0:hi>Moses?</ns0:hi> It is easily answered, That even the five Books of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> make mention of the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> under the Notion of <ns0:hi>the S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ed of the Woman,</ns0:hi> Gen. 3.15. the <ns0:hi>Seed of Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> Gen. 49.10. The <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> like to <ns0:hi>Moses, Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.15. And for the name <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> she might easily learn it from other <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that the Person called <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> was called by <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Jesus saith unto her,<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> I that speak unto thee am <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">That same <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> of whom thou declarest thy self to have some expectation, and from whom thou expectest to hear all things necessary to Salvation. Some here en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quire, why our Saviour maketh to this Woman such a plain Discovery of himself, when as we find him in the Gospel so cautious, and so often charging his Disciples not to make him known. Some think our Saviour thus gratified the Honesty and Simplicity which he discerned in this Woman, not coming to catch him, but to be Instructed from him; but possibly if we wistly consider those Texts wherein he charged his Disciples not to make him known, we shall find that the thing which he cautioned them against, was their publishing of him <ns0:hi>as the Son of God,</ns0:hi> which our Saviour desired should be concealed, till he should be so <ns0:hi>declared with power by his Resurrection from the Dead,</ns0:hi> Rom. 1.4. that his Enemies by a charge of <ns0:hi>Blasphemy</ns0:hi> against him, might not cut him off before his hour was come. Now, we shall observe that the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> tho' they expected a <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> yet had no such Notion of him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:336" />27 And upon this, came his Disciples <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">They, as we heard before, were gone into the City <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi> to buy Food, and were kept there by the Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence of God till our Saviour had finished this Discourse with the Woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> but came after the Discourse was done;</ns0:note>, and marvelled that he talked with the woman <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">they marvelled possibly at his talking with a Woman in the Road (a thing forbidden by their Tradi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions) especially a Woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> with whom the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had no Commerce</ns0:note>, yet no man said, what seekest thou? or why talkest thou with her <ns0:note n="z." place="bottom">But yet they had so much Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verence and Respect for their Master, that they enquired not curiously into the matter or reason of his Discourse.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 The Woman then left her water pot, and went her way into the City <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">She had no sooner tasted of the Living water spoken of by Christ, but she left her Water-pot: Thus <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> tells our Saviour, that <ns0:hi>they had left all and followed him.</ns0:hi> She goeth into the City <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi> (no doubt) or <ns0:hi>Sychar,</ns0:hi> men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 5.</ns0:note>, and saith unto the men <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">and doth not her self enter into a long Discourse with the Citizens, onely inviteth the <ns0:hi>Citizens</ns0:hi> to come and see Christ, that they might judge from the hearing of their own Ears, and the sight of their own Eyes.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Come see a man, which told me all things that ever I did <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">She invites them to him under the Notion of a Man, who had told her <ns0:hi>all things that she ever did.</ns0:hi> Christ doubtless had told her, and spoken to her, much more than <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> hath left us upon Sacred Record; yet not <ns0:hi>all things</ns0:hi> she ever did, but <ns0:hi>all things</ns0:hi> (as often) signifies many things, and those such things as she might know that he who could tell those things, could have told her <ns0:hi>all things</ns0:hi> if they had been so proper for him to have repeated to her, as those things which he did tell her.</ns0:note>, is not this the Christ <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This induced her to believe, that he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> she offereth it to their Opinion and Judgment.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Then they went out of the City, and came unto him <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Sitting still at the Well, they (many of them at least) did not contemn the News as the Relation of a Woman, but went (possibly but out of Curiosity) to see, and to hear this Man.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 In the mean while his Disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Whiles the Woman was fetching her Citizens to come and see, and hear Christ, his Disciples knowing that he must be weary and hungry with his Journey, and having brought him some Food out of the City, where they had been to fetch it, they put him upon refreshing himself with the Food they had brought.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">But our Blessed Lord was more intent upon Gospel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lizing the <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> than satisfying his Hunger; what this Meat was, he opens himself, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 34.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Therefore said the Disciples one to ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, Hath any man brought him <ns0:hi>ought</ns0:hi> to eat <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">His Disciples being yet Carnal, did not understand him, but thought that he had spoken of Bodily Nourish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment. See the like Instances, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 16.7. and <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.11. they were wondring how he came by meat, and who should bring it him: So hard are we to conceive of Spiritual things, till God openeth our Eyes.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">Our Lord, without any reproof of them for their dulness in understanding, and having compassion on their Infirmity and Ignorance, tells them what he meant by his former words; telling them, that the doing of his <ns0:hi>Fathers Will,</ns0:hi> and the finishing of his Work, was that which he more hungred after, and took more delight in, than in eating and drinking; this is what he sought, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.30. that which he came down from Heaven for, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.38. As the Law of God was sweeter to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> than the <ns0:hi>Hony,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Hony-comb,</ns0:hi> so the publishing of the Gospel was to Jesus Christ,</ns0:note>, and to finish his work <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">the calling Sinners to Repentance, and pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lishing the glad tidings of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; that was his work, which he tells his Father he had finished, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 17.4. Here<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by teaching Ministers and People also, to prefer Spiritual things before Temporal, and the Ministers of the Gospel especially to prefer the publishing of the Gospel (which is their work) to any other employment whatsoever.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Say not ye, There are yet four Months<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>then</ns0:hi> cometh Harvest <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">There was in those Countreys but four Months space betwixt <ns0:hi>Seed-time</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Harvest</ns0:hi>: Yet they fed themselves (as soon as they had sown) with the expectation of it</ns0:note>: Behold<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I say unto you, lift up your Eyes, and look on the Fields <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">My Harvest, saith our Saviour, is the gaining of Souls for my Father; look yonder what a Troop of the Citizens of <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi> are coming to me, upon my Revelation of my self to the Woman of <ns0:hi>Samaria</ns0:hi>: I have but just sown my Seed</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 10.2.</ns0:note> for they are white already to Harvest <ns0:note n="m," place="bottom">and the Fields are white to this Spiritual Harvest, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.37. In the judgment of the best Interpreters, our Saviour in this Verse useth a comparison, and passeth from his Simi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litude used in the former part of the Verse, fetched from a Worldly Harvest, to discourse of that Spiritual Harvest, which he by and by Reaped of the Citizens of <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to him; it is of that he saith, that the Fields were al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ready <ns0:hi>white,</ns0:hi> by which (as will appear from the following Verses) he quickneth his Disciples to put in their Sickles. Some Critical Authors, understanding both the former and latter part of the Text of a Worldly Harvest, have used their Wits to determine how the Fields should be <ns0:hi>white to Harvest</ns0:hi> four Months before it came; but the most and best Interpreters Interpret the latter part, of a Spiritual Harvest, and that will be also justified by what followeth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And he that reapeth receiveth wages <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">You that are the Lords Instruments, to reap what the Prophets of old, and <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> lately have sown, shall not lose your labour, you shall receive wages</ns0:note>, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal <ns0:note n="o," place="bottom">and your wages shall not be small, it shall be no less than Eternal life, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>They that turn many to Righteousness, shall shine as the Stars for ever and ever</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, that both he that soweth, and he that reapeth, may rejoyce together <ns0:note n="p." place="bottom">Thus the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> who sowed the Seed of the Gospel, and you that succeed them, and reap the fruit of what they did sow, shall have the same reward in Glory, and reioyce together. <ns0:hi>The Plow-man shall overtake the Reaper, and the treader of Grapes him that soweth Seed</ns0:hi> (as <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> speaks) <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 9.13. This Text is of great use to those Godly Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters which faithfully sow the Seed of the Word, but do not in their Life-time see any great effects of it; it may be it comes up when they are in their Graves; the Reward of a faithful Preacher doth not depend upon his success in his Labours, but upon his faithful discharge of his Work; tho' one soweth and another reapeth, yet both he that soweth, and he that reapeth shall reioyce together.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">It was a Proverbial expression, most commonly used with reference to those who unjustly invaded the Rights and Possessions of other men; but as applicable unto those who by the disposing Providence of God, rightly Inherit the Fruit of other mens Labours, as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> Inherited the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 24.13. <ns0:hi>A land for which ye did not labour, and Cities which ye built not.</ns0:hi> This saying (saith our Saviour) is fulfilled in you.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 I sent you to reap that whereon you be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stowed no labour <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">I have sent you to reap that which you did not first la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour for</ns0:note>; other men laboured, and ye are entred into their labours <ns0:note n="s:" place="bottom">the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and my self, have sown the Seed, and by their Doctrine prepared for the Lord a People; you enter upon their Labours, ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thering them into a Gospel Church.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And many of the Samaritans of that City believed on him, for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">That City was <ns0:hi>Sichem,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sychar,</ns0:hi> but it was within the Province of <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> from whence it is that they had the name of <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> as well as <ns0:hi>Sichemites</ns0:hi>: Many of them upon the Testimony of the Woman, That he had told her such secret passages of her Life, as he could not have told her, if he had not been able, if he had pleased, as well to have told her all things, <ns0:hi>believed on him</ns0:hi>: That is, they owned him as a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> and agreed to what the Woman said in that particular, and were by it excited to come to see, and further discourse with Christ. This justifieth what our Saviour said, That there was there a People prepared for the Lord, the Fields were white unto the Harvest; that they were thus far wrought upon by the Discourse of a Woman, and she one not of the higest Reputation, and onely telling them, That he had told her all things she had done. Small means have great effects, when Gods time of working is come.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:337" />40 So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Sichemites</ns0:hi> being come to Christ, had some Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />course with him, as appeareth from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 41, 42. What the subject-matter of their Discourse was, we are not told; we may know that it was Spiritual, and something proper to excite Faith in them; for believing was the effect of it; they desire that he would abide with them: thus their Faith wrought by Love</ns0:note>. And he abode there two days <ns0:note n="w." place="bottom">Our Saviour, that he might not dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courage the beginning of their Faith, did stay with them two days: For altho when he sent out his Disciples, he commanded them not to go into the way of the <ns0:hi>Samari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tans,</ns0:hi> yet himself was not obliged by that Law, and did sometimes by Preaching to Heathens, and Converting of them, give an Earnest of the Calling of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> whose fuller Calling was reserved to after times, yet probably, the reason why he would not stay longer with them than two days, was because the time was not yet come, for the fuller Calling of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and he was not willing by a longer abode with them to give offence to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt whom and the <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> was a rooted Hatred up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the account of their differing Religion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And many mo believed, because of his own word <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Believing</ns0:hi> seemeth here to be taken in a different sense from what it was taken in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39. from what followeth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42. There it seemeth onely to signifie a lower degree of assent, that he was a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> upon the womans saying, That he had told her all she had done; here it signifieth a giving Credit to him, as the Christ, the Saviour of the World, of which they were convinced by what they heard from himself. Thus that of the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.17. is justified, <ns0:hi>That faith cometh by hearing</ns0:hi>; and the Influence of Christ upon the Souls of Believers is also justified: We read of no Miracles our Saviour wrought here, they <ns0:hi>believed</ns0:hi> not because of any Signs they saw, but because of his word, wherein also they further shewed themselves the <ns0:hi>first fruit of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> the generality of which were afterward Converted to the Faith of the Gospel, after that Miracles were ceased, by hearing the Gospel Preached.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And said unto the woman, Now we be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve, not because of thy saying <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Several things may be the occasion of Faith, which are neither the principal efficient causes, nor the proper instrumental cause of it: The principal efficient cause of the Faith of these <ns0:hi>Samaritans,</ns0:hi> was undoubtedly the finger of God upon their Souls, enlightning their minds with the saving knowledge of the Gospel, and bowing their wills to the Obedience of it. The proper instrumental cause was their hearing the words of Christ, but the <ns0:hi>Occasion</ns0:hi> of this was what the Woman had told them; so as, tho they in a sense <ns0:hi>believed</ns0:hi> because of what she had said, because that occasioned their coming out to see, and hear Christ; yet the proper instrumental cause was their hearing Christ, God upon their hearing him working in their hearts, an ability, and a willingness to receive and to close with Christ. Thus the <ns0:hi>Church</ns0:hi> gives us the first occasion of receiving the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures, and believing them to be the Word of God, we having them put into our hands by the Church, read them, and find such impresses and stamps of Divinity in them, that we conclude from our Reason very probably, that they are more than Humane Writings, but never firmly and fixedly receive them as such, until persuaded of it by the Holy Spirit.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 17.8.</ns0:note> we have heard him our selves, and know that this is in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed the Christ, the Saviour of the world <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">These <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> do not onely own Christ as a <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> nor do they onely <ns0:hi>suspect</ns0:hi> that he must be the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> but they profess to know, that he was the Christ, the <ns0:hi>Saviour of the World.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 Now after two days, he departed thence, and went into Galilee <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Christ (as we heard before, <ns0:hi>Ver.</ns0:hi> 3.) was upon his Journey into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> onely he stopt two days at <ns0:hi>Sichem</ns0:hi> to gratifie the desires of the <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> of that City, which two days being now spent, he keepeth on in his Journey: But here ariseth a Question, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> Whether he first went to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> or to <ns0:hi>Cana</ns0:hi>; for the Opinion of those, who think he first went to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> is quoted <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 4.12. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides it is said, that <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> was in his Road to <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.24. he is said to have uttered these words there. <ns0:hi>Chemnitius</ns0:hi> thinks he went first to <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> according to what <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> relateth in the following Verses. And <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.16. he is said to have gone out of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi>; and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides, the next mentioned Miracle is <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 5. said to have been Christs Second Miracle, which it could not have been, had he first gone to <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi>; for <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.23. those of <ns0:hi>Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zareth</ns0:hi> mention some Miracles which he had wrought at <ns0:hi>Capernaum.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 For Jesus himself testified, that a Prophet hath no honour in his own Countrey <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Christ spake those words more than once, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 13.57. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 6.4. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.24. But the Question is, what force of Reason this hath, why he went into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> when as <ns0:hi>Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zareth,</ns0:hi> which was in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> was his own Countrey; for tho he was Born in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> yet he was Educated at <ns0:hi>Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zareth</ns0:hi>; upon which account, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.23. it is called <ns0:hi>his own Countrey?</ns0:hi> The best Resolution of this Difficulty is, That by <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> here is to be understood, the Country-part of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> exclusive to <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi>; and this is not given as a Reason why our Saviour went into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> but why he did not go to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> but into the Country-part of <ns0:hi>Ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lilee,</ns0:hi> because <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> was his own Countrey, <ns0:hi>and a Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet is not without honour, except in his own Countrey.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Hierusalem at the feast <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">When he came not to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> but to some parts of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Galileans</ns0:hi> entertained him Hospitably, and this they did because of those Miracles they had seen wrought by him at the <ns0:hi>Passeover-feast,</ns0:hi> where Christ was, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.</ns0:note>; for they also went unto the feast <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">For these <ns0:hi>Galileans,</ns0:hi> tho they lived at a great distance from <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> yet were observant of the Law which com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded all the Males of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> to be present at that So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lemnity. The <ns0:hi>Samaritans</ns0:hi> saw no Miracle, but believed Christ upon his word: The <ns0:hi>Galileans</ns0:hi> also received Christ, but their seeing of his Miracles at the Feast, is given as the cause of their receiving him, their Faith was not so noble as that of the <ns0:hi>Samaritans. Blessed</ns0:hi> (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>are they, who have not seen, and yet believed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>p. 2.1, 11.</ns0:note> where he made the water wine <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Our Saviour, coming into <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> made choice of <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> the place where being at a Marriage-feast, he turned Water into Wine <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2, first to fix in; the reason is not expressed, and therefore vainly guessed at by <ns0:hi>Interpreters,</ns0:hi> there he worketh a Second Miracle, not upon the Person of any one of <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> but upon the Son of one who was at <ns0:hi>Capernaum,</ns0:hi> which was a City in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Naphtali</ns0:hi> upon the Shoar of the Famous River <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>. And there was a certain <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or Courtier, or Ruler, 'tis</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Nobleman, whose Son was sick at Capernaum <ns0:note n="f:" place="bottom">This Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son is described to be one that was <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, a <ns0:hi>Nobleman,</ns0:hi> whether of the Blood of <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> that was <ns0:hi>Tetrarch of Ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lilee,</ns0:hi> or some Courtier, or Principal Servant of his, it is not said.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judea into Galilee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Christ had been in <ns0:hi>Ga<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ee</ns0:hi> before, and in this Town, and wrought a Miracle, and if this <ns0:hi>Courtier</ns0:hi> were a Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> (which some think, but it is hard to prove) it is probable he had been at the Passeover, and seen the Miracles he wrought there, or at least might have heard of them from some who were there</ns0:note>, he went unto him and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sought him that he would come down and heal his Son <ns0:note n="h," place="bottom">though it was a good way from <ns0:hi>Capernaum</ns0:hi> thither, yet his love to his Son car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried him, and humbled him to beseech Christ, that he would come down and heal his Son, by which he shewed a great weakness of Faith, as if he thought that Christ could not put forth his Healing Vertue at a distance, but his Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sonal Presence was necessary, as <ns0:hi>Naaman</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Syrian</ns0:hi> thought that <ns0:hi>Elisha</ns0:hi> must come down and lay his hand upon him</ns0:note>; for he was at the point of death <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">his Son it seems was in Humane appearance dying.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 Then said Jesus unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 1.22.</ns0:note> except ye see signs and wonders, you will not believe <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">It may seem strange to such as do not well weigh all Circumstances, that our Saviour, who at other times went without asking, shewed himself so hard to be intreated by this Courtier, and answereth him so roughly; but we must not take our selves to be able to give a certain Account of all Christs Actions, and different dealings with Persons, whose Hearts he well enough knew. Thus much is certain, that our Saviour always preferred that Faith which was gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven to his bare word, before that which waited for a Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racle confirmative of that word, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 20.29. Our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour saw that this <ns0:hi>Courtier</ns0:hi> came to him purely upon a Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural account, for the Recovery of his dying Son, without a desire to be Instructed in his Heavenly Doctrine, therefore (as it may be presumed) he checks this <ns0:hi>Courtier,</ns0:hi> and not him alone, but the generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who were onely struck with Admiration of his works, and drawn from Curiosity, or some Temporal benefit, to follow him, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out a due regard of his Person, or the Heavenly saving Truths Preached by him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:337" />49 The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, Come down, ere my child dye <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The Courtier, tho probably of Spirit enough to have shewn some discontent at our Saviours no kinder Answer to him before, yet was so intent upon his Sons life, that he takes no notice of it, but reneweth his Request, still dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covering the weakness of his Faith, as thinking that Christs Personal Presence was necessary to the life of his Son.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Our Saviour would neither discourage the weak Faith of this Nobleman, nor yet incourage his weakness, he healeth his Son for the encouragement of his Faith, he doth it by his word, without going down to him, that he might not gratifie his weakness, thinking his Personal Presence was necessary; he bids him go, for his Son was recovered (that is here meant by <ns0:hi>liveth</ns0:hi>;)</ns0:note>. And the man believed the word that Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus had spoken unto him, and he went his way <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">upon this his Faith grow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, and he who before onely believed Christ to be a Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet probably upon others hearsay, now believeth his word, that is, was persuaded that his Son was indeed Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covered.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> saying, Thy son liveth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The servants that met him to bring the acceptable News of his Sons recovery, knew nothing of the passages that had been betwixt Christ and their Master, but merely came to tell their Master, what they knew would be ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptable to him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 Then enquired he the hour when he began to amend: and they said unto him, yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">He enquireth the precise time, they tell him it was about the seventh hour. The Miracle appeared in the sud<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />denness of the Recovery, and also that it was without the application of means, at least any that could have pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duced so sudden an effect.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 So the father knew that <ns0:hi>it was</ns0:hi> at the same hour in which Jesus had said unto him, Thy son liveth <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The circumstance of the time when his Son recovered agreeing with the very hour, when Christ had said unto him, <ns0:hi>Thy son liveth,</ns0:hi> was a mighty confirmation to him, that he was beholden to Christ for his Cure, and conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently, that Christ was no ordinary man, more than a Prophet, even the Son of God;</ns0:note>, and himself believed, and his whole house <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">this works upon his Faith to an higher degree: He first believed the report of him, then he gave credit to the word that he spake, now he believeth savingly, and not he alone, but his whole Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mily became Christians. Such Instances we have concern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:hi>Lydia,</ns0:hi> Acts 16.14, 15. the <ns0:hi>Iaylour, v.</ns0:hi> 34. and <ns0:hi>Crispus,</ns0:hi> Acts 18.8.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 This <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> again the second miracle <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> Jesus did, when he was come out of Judea into Ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lilee <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">His turning Water into Wine, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2. was the first, this was the second, and so in order of time before any of those Miracles which he wrought in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> of which we read, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 4.23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
